blocks.prompt: 6 (i) If \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) are the angles of a triangle \(ABC\), then prove that \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\gamma\)
blocks.explanation:
Triangle ke teeno angles ka jama hamesha \(180^{\circ}\) hota hai; yahi is sawal ki chaabi hai.
Diya kya hai? \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) triangle ke angles hain. Prove kya karna hai? \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\gamma\).
Plan: \(\alpha + \beta\) ko \(180^{\circ} - \gamma\) likhna, phir \(\sin(180^{\circ} - \theta) = \sin\theta\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) triangle \(ABC\) ke angles hain, is liye \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\).
Humein prove karna hai: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\gamma\).
Tareeqa: Jo do angles jure hue hain un ko teesre angle ki madad se likhenge (kyunke teeno ka jama \(180^{\circ}\) hai), phir allied angle ka rule lagayenge.

\(\alpha + \beta\) ko \(\gamma\) mein likhein
\[\alpha + \beta = 180^{\circ} - \gamma\]
Kyun: \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\) ke dono taraf se \(\gamma\) minus kiya. Ab do angles ka jama ek allied angle ban gaya.

Allied angle ka rule lagayein
\[\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin(180^{\circ} - \gamma)\]
\[= \sin\gamma\]
Kyun: \(180^{\circ}\) even multiple hai, is liye sin sin hi raha. \(180^{\circ} - \gamma\) quadrant II mein hai (agar \(\gamma\) acute ho), aur wahan sin positive hai. \(\gamma\) obtuse ho to yeh quadrant I mein hoga, phir bhi sin positive. Is liye har triangle mein sach.

Tasdeeq: equilateral triangle se
\[\alpha = \beta = \gamma = 60^{\circ}\]
\[\sin 120^{\circ} = \sin 60^{\circ} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Barabar sides wale triangle mein har angle \(60^{\circ}\) hai. Left side \(\sin 120^{\circ}\) aur right side \(\sin 60^{\circ}\), dono \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 6 (ii) If \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) are the angles of a triangle \(ABC\), then prove that \(\sec\left(\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\right) = \csc\frac{\gamma}{2}\)
blocks.explanation:
Is part mein adhe angles hain. Triangle ke angles ka jama \(180^{\circ}\) hai, to un ka aadha \(90^{\circ}\) hoga.
Diya kya hai? \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\). Prove kya karna hai? \(\sec\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2} = \csc\frac{\gamma}{2}\). (\(\csc\) cosec hi ka doosra naam hai.)
Plan: \(\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2} = 90^{\circ} - \frac{\gamma}{2}\) likhna, phir co-ratio ka rule.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) triangle \(ABC\) ke angles hain, is liye \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\).
Humein prove karna hai: \(\sec\left(\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\right) = \csc\frac{\gamma}{2}\).
Tareeqa: Jo do angles jure hue hain un ko teesre angle ki madad se likhenge (kyunke teeno ka jama \(180^{\circ}\) hai), phir allied angle ka rule lagayenge.

Angles ke jame ko aadha karein
\[\dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2} = \dfrac{180^{\circ} - \gamma}{2}\]
\[= 90^{\circ} - \dfrac{\gamma}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\alpha + \beta = 180^{\circ} - \gamma\). Dono terms ko 2 se divide kiya: \(180 \div 2 = 90\) aur \(\gamma \div 2 = \frac{\gamma}{2}\).

Co-ratio ka rule lagayein
\[\sec\left(90^{\circ} - \tfrac{\gamma}{2}\right) = \operatorname{cosec}\tfrac{\gamma}{2}\]
Kyun: \(90^{\circ}\) odd multiple hai, is liye sec badal kar us ka co-ratio cosec ban gaya. \(\gamma\) triangle ka angle hai, \(180^{\circ}\) se chhota, is liye \(\frac{\gamma}{2}\) \(90^{\circ}\) se chhota; angle quadrant I mein hai aur sign positive.

Tasdeeq: \(\gamma = 60^{\circ}\) le kar
\[\sec 60^{\circ} = 2\]
\[\operatorname{cosec} 30^{\circ} = 2 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\gamma = 60^{\circ}\) ho to \(\alpha + \beta = 120^{\circ}\) aur us ka aadha \(60^{\circ}\). Left side \(\sec 60^{\circ} = 2\), right side \(\operatorname{cosec} 30^{\circ} = 2\). Barabar.

blocks.prompt: 6 (iii) If \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) are the angles of a triangle \(ABC\), then prove that \(\operatorname{cosec}\alpha = \frac{1}{\sin(\beta + \gamma)}\)
blocks.explanation:
Is dafa jora \(\beta + \gamma\) hai, aur right side par us ka sin neeche hai.
Diya kya hai? \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\). Prove kya karna hai? \(\operatorname{cosec}\alpha = \frac{1}{\sin(\beta + \gamma)}\).
Plan: pehle dikhayenge ke \(\sin(\beta + \gamma) = \sin\alpha\), phir dono ka ulta (reciprocal) lenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) triangle \(ABC\) ke angles hain, is liye \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\).
Humein prove karna hai: \(\operatorname{cosec}\alpha = \frac{1}{\sin(\beta + \gamma)}\).
Tareeqa: Jo do angles jure hue hain un ko teesre angle ki madad se likhenge (kyunke teeno ka jama \(180^{\circ}\) hai), phir allied angle ka rule lagayenge.

\(\beta + \gamma\) ko \(\alpha\) mein likhein
\[\beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ} - \alpha\]
Kyun: \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\) mein se \(\alpha\) dono taraf se minus kiya.

\(\sin(\beta + \gamma)\) nikalein
\[\sin(\beta + \gamma) = \sin(180^{\circ} - \alpha)\]
\[= \sin\alpha\]
Kyun: Even multiple, sin sin hi raha. \(180^{\circ} - \alpha\) quadrant I ya II mein hai, dono jagah sin positive.

Ulta (reciprocal) lein
\[\dfrac{1}{\sin(\beta + \gamma)} = \dfrac{1}{\sin\alpha}\]
\[= \operatorname{cosec}\alpha\]
Kyun: Jab do cheezein barabar hon to un ke ulte bhi barabar hote hain. Cosec, sin ka ulta hai. Triangle ka angle \(0^{\circ}\) aur \(180^{\circ}\) ke darmiyan hota hai, is liye \(\sin\alpha\) kabhi zero nahi hota aur divide karna jaiz hai.

blocks.prompt: 6 (iv) If \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) are the angles of a triangle \(ABC\), then prove that \(\tan(\alpha + \beta) + \tan\gamma = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan bhi wohi chaabi: \(\alpha + \beta = 180^{\circ} - \gamma\).
Diya kya hai? Triangle ke angles. Prove kya karna hai? \(\tan(\alpha + \beta) + \tan\gamma = 0\), yani \(\tan(\alpha + \beta) = -\tan\gamma\).
Plan: \(\tan(180^{\circ} - \theta) = -\tan\theta\) lagana, phir jama.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) triangle \(ABC\) ke angles hain, is liye \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\).
Humein prove karna hai: \(\tan(\alpha + \beta) + \tan\gamma = 0\).
Tareeqa: Jo do angles jure hue hain un ko teesre angle ki madad se likhenge (kyunke teeno ka jama \(180^{\circ}\) hai), phir allied angle ka rule lagayenge.

\(\alpha + \beta\) ko \(\gamma\) mein likhein
\[\alpha + \beta = 180^{\circ} - \gamma\]
Kyun: Teeno angles ka jama \(180^{\circ}\) hai.

Allied angle ka rule lagayein
\[\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \tan(180^{\circ} - \gamma)\]
\[= -\tan\gamma\]
Kyun: \(180^{\circ}\) even multiple, tan tan hi raha. \(\gamma\) acute ho to \(180^{\circ} - \gamma\) quadrant II mein hai jahan tan negative hai, is liye minus. Yahi minus sawal ka asal nukta hai.

\(\tan\gamma\) jama karein
\[\tan(\alpha + \beta) + \tan\gamma = -\tan\gamma + \tan\gamma\]
\[= 0\]
Kyun: Ek hi cheez ek dafa minus aur ek dafa plus, is liye zero.
Dhyan dein: agar \(\gamma = 90^{\circ}\) ho to \(\tan 90^{\circ}\) defined hi nahi, is liye yeh result right angle ke liye nahi likha ja sakta. Exam mein yeh baat ek line mein likh dena achha hai.
